stem: The elements in Group 2, and their compounds, show many similarities and trends in their properties.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem: Magnesium, calcium, strontium and barium all react with cold water.
parts.text: Describe what you would **see** when some calcium is added to cold water.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Write an equation for the reaction taking place in **(i)**.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Describe how the reaction of barium with cold water would differ from the reaction of calcium in **(i)** in terms of what you would **see**.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: Magnesium oxide can be formed by the reaction of magnesium and oxygen in the air.
parts.text:
Draw a **fully labelled** reaction pathway diagram for the reaction between magnesium and oxygen.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why there is no visible reaction when a piece of magnesium ribbon is exposed to the air.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
Magnesium oxide is used to manufacture heat-resistant bricks for furnace linings in the steel-making industry.

State and explain the property of magnesium oxide that makes it suitable for this use.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text: Suggest a reason why magnesium oxide cannot be used as a lining for any furnaces containing acidic materials.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: The nitrates and carbonates of the Group 2 elements, from magnesium to barium, decompose when heated.
parts.text: State the trend in the temperature of thermal decomposition of these Group 2 nitrates and carbonates.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Give the equation for the thermal decomposition of magnesium carbonate.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Give the equation for the thermal decomposition of calcium nitrate.
